newsitem.title: USA: US consumer confidence 118.5 in Mar vs rvsd 118.9.
newsitem.headline: US consumer confidence 118.5 in Mar vs rvsd 118.9.

text.p: The index of U.S. consumer confidence slipped to 118.5 in March, down from a revised reading of 118.9 in February, the Conference Board said on Tuesday.
The present situation component fell slightly to 144.1 in March from a revised reading of 144.3 in February, but it continues to run at a 27-year high, the Conference Board said.
Meanwhile, the expectations component of the March index edged down to 101.4 from a revised 101.9 in February, it said.

The report said consumers are "more positive about current job prospects than they were in February," as more than 33 percent of the surveyed households said jobs are "plentiful" today, up from 32.5 percent in February.
"Despite some concerns about an economic moderation ahead, consumer confidence continues to run at relatively high levels," said Lynn Franco, associate director of The Consumer Research Center.
Franco said the message from consumers is that "both business and employment conditions will remain upbeat through the spring and the summer."

The survey found the biggest gains in confidence over the last three months versus the same period a year ago have been in the Middle Atlantic states. The smallest gains have been in the Mountain states, the Conference Board said.
